Maya Chen: FYI — BigCorp asked that RLHF-style evals be part of their onboarding benchmark. They want a canary where the model only goes GA for them after passing RLHF safety/quality checks. Can we define an exception flow?
Liam O'Connor: curious: do they mean we run their reward model on our infra or they provide eval harness + labels?
Maya Chen: they will provide an internal reward model + a small labeled holdout. Privacy consent exists but they want the run on our Dedicated cluster.
Raj Patel: ok security implications aside, this is more than our usual perf/accuracy checks. Suggest flow: 1) standard automated bench (latency, throughput, tox), 2) client RLHF harness run in isolated env, 3) manual QA signoff if RLHF disagrees with automated metrics, 4) pin until periodic re-eval.
Sophia Varela: cost/ops question: RLHF harness runs can be expensive and longer. Need to set timeboxes and SLOs so onboarding doesn't stall other customers. What are acceptable thresholds?
Maya Chen: customer expects pass within 2 weeks, otherwise they want rollback/opt-out. They also require we keep a pinned variant for 90 days post-GA.
Liam O'Connor: proposed gated criteria (rough sketch):
```
- Functional: no major regression on core intents (>99% intent coverage)
- Quality: client reward-model delta <= 0.03 relative to their baseline (higher-is-better)
- Safety: automated toxicity filters + manual audit for top 100 failure cases
- Performance: 95th p90 latency within our Dedicated SLO or customer pays for burst
- Cost: RLHF run < X GPU-hours (we'll quantify)
```
Raj Patel: ops notes: we MUST run the harness in a tenant-isolated namespace, volume-scrub logs, and return only aggregate metrics to the customer. We can't keep their reward model in long-term storage.
Sophia Varela: product asks: add launch gates to catalog entry meta: `rlhf_required`, `rlhf_pass_ts`, `pinned_until`, `rlhf_owner`. This will help Console visibility and billing.
Maya Chen: agree. Also need a stopgap: if the RLHF harness is flaky, we allow a `provisional-GA` for non-critical routes for 14 days while we debug.
Liam O'Connor: who owns the run? infra + eng-ml pairing. Raj can you estimate infra changes (isolation + ephemeral GPU quota)?
Raj Patel: rough estimate: ~2 days infra design, ~1 week to provision namespace + quota + scrub pipeline. Add ~3 engineer-days for integration tests.
Sophia Varela: I'll model the cost impact and propose a chargeback for customer-covered RLHF runs. Will share numbers by EOD Thu.
Maya Chen: action items:
- Raj: infra design + estimate doc (due Tue)
- Liam: define the RLHF pass spec with metrics and sample size (due Wed)
- Sophia: pricing/chargeback proposal (due Thu EOD)
- Maya: draft product-side onboarding playbook and metadata fields (due Fri)
infra-bot: CI: #rlhf-harness-infra build passed — 1 job, 0 failures (:white_check_mark:)
Liam O'Connor: +1 to the timeline. Also let's add an explicit rollback clause in the onboarding contract.
Maya Chen: noted. I'll loop in legal and account exec after next sync.
Sophia Varela: can someone add this to the catalog onboarding checklist as an optional gate `RLHF_OVERRIDE`? small doc PR would be perfect.
Raj Patel: I'll create a draft infra PR today and tag reviewers.
Maya Chen: thanks team. Will run a short sync tomorrow 09:30 PT to align owners. :calendar: :white_check_mark:
